modules.name: T1DM vs. T2DM and the Death of Sliding Scale Monotherapy
Designing and Titrating Subcutaneous Insulin Regimens
Safe Transitions of Care and Resident Ward Cases

slides.title: The Inpatient Burden of Dysglycemia and Curriculum Roadmap
bullets: Hyperglycemia above 140 mg/dL affects 32%-38% of non-ICU patients and 40%-50% of ICU patients.
Inpatient dysglycemia follows a U-shaped mortality curve driven by severe hyperglycemia above 200 mg/dL and hypoglycemia below 70 mg/dL.
Three inpatient phenotypes exist: known diabetes, undiagnosed diabetes (HbA1c >= 6.5%), and stress hyperglycemia (HbA1c < 6.5%).
Six modules cover targets, basal-bolus dosing, high-risk scenarios, 2024 DKA/HHS updates, and safe discharge.
slides.speaker_notes: Evidence Base: Umpierrez et al. (J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2002) showed newly discovered inpatient hyperglycemia carried an 18-fold higher in-hospital mortality (16%) versus normoglycemia (1.7%) and higher mortality than known diabetes (3%). Attending Pearl: Stress to PGY-1s that stress hyperglycemia is not benign; it impairs neutrophil chemotaxis, phagocytosis, and complement activation, increasing surgical site and nosocomial infections.

slides.title: Pathophysiology of Inpatient Hyperglycemia
bullets: Acute illness surges cortisol, epinephrine, glucagon, and growth hormone, driving hepatic gluconeogenesis and peripheral insulin resistance.
Pro-inflammatory cytokines TNF-alpha and IL-6 blunt skeletal muscle GLUT4 translocation and worsen insulin resistance.
Iatrogenic triggers include glucocorticoids, catecholamine vasopressors, dextrose IV fluids, enteral/parenteral nutrition, and calcineurin inhibitors.
Hyperglycemia causes oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, platelet activation, and osmotic diuresis with electrolyte wasting.
slides.speaker_notes: Evidence Base: Mechanistic clinical studies confirm lowering BG below 180 mg/dL restores neutrophil oxidative burst capacity and reduces microvascular endothelial injury. Attending Pearl: As acute infection or inflammation resolves, counter-regulatory hormones drop rapidly. Failing to proactively down-titrate insulin as steroids taper or sepsis resolves is a primary driver of late-hospitalization hypoglycemia.

slides.title: Evolution of Glycemic Targets: From Leuven to NICE-SUGAR
bullets: Leuven I (2001, n=1,548 surgical ICU) showed intensive IV insulin (80-110 mg/dL) reduced mortality from 8.0% to 4.6%.
Leuven II (2006, n=1,200 medical ICU) showed no mortality benefit and 6-fold higher severe hypoglycemia (18.7% vs. 3.1%).
NICE-SUGAR (2009, n=6,104) compared 81-108 mg/dL versus < 180 mg/dL across medical and surgical ICUs.
Intensive control in NICE-SUGAR increased 90-day mortality (27.5% vs. 24.9%, p=0.02) and severe hypoglycemia < 40 mg/dL (6.8% vs. 0.5%).

chart_spec.title: NICE-SUGAR (n = 6,104): Intensive vs. Conventional ICU Targets

slides.speaker_notes: Evidence Base: NICE-SUGAR Investigators (NEJM 2009) permanently shifted global inpatient practice away from tight normoglycemia toward moderate, hypoglycemia-safe targets. Attending Pearl: Ask PGY-2/3 residents why Leuven I differed from NICE-SUGAR: Leuven I used aggressive early parenteral dextrose nutrition creating artificial hyperglycemia in controls, arterial sampling, and a single specialized surgical unit.

slides.title: Current Glycemic Targets and Admission Diagnostic Workup
bullets: Initiate insulin for persistent hyperglycemia >= 180 mg/dL on two occasions within 24 hours.
Check admission HbA1c for all diabetes or hyperglycemia (> 140 mg/dL) patients without a result in the past 3 months.
Obtain baseline BMP (creatinine, eGFR, potassium, bicarbonate) and accurate body weight in kilograms on admission.

table.title: ADA 2024-2025 & Endocrine Society 2022 Glycemic Targets
rows: Use validated IV insulin protocol; 110-140 mg/dL only if low hypoglycemia risk
Endocrine Society notes pre-meal < 140 mg/dL and random < 180 mg/dL
Purely to prevent osmotic symptoms and dehydration

slides.speaker_notes: Evidence Base: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes (2024/2025, Section 16) and Endocrine Society 2022 Guideline. Attending Pearl: Point out that HbA1c may be falsely low after recent blood transfusion, acute blood loss, hemolysis, erythropoietin therapy, or ESRD with shortened RBC lifespan. Always interpret HbA1c in clinical context.

slides.title: Type 1 vs. Type 2 Diabetes in the Hospital: The Absolute Basal Rule
bullets: T1DM involves absolute beta-cell destruction; continuous basal insulin is mandatory to suppress lipolysis and ketogenesis.
NEVER withhold basal insulin completely in T1DM, even if NPO or mildly hypoglycemic, or DKA develops within 4-8 hours.
Long-standing insulinopenic T2DM can behave like T1DM and develop DKA if basal insulin is abruptly omitted.
Pancreatogenic diabetes (Type 3c) lacks both insulin and glucagon, causing brittle glycemic swings and severe hypoglycemia.
slides.speaker_notes: Evidence Base: ADA Standards of Care (2024/2025) and Joint British Diabetes Societies (JBDS) Inpatient Safety Guidelines. Attending Pearl: Teach the T1DM Safety Reflex: If a T1DM patient has a morning BG of 85 mg/dL and is NPO, do NOT hold basal insulin. Reduce the basal dose by 20% and initiate dextrose-containing maintenance IV fluids (e.g., D5 1/2 NS at 75-100 mL/hr) to safely cover basal insulin.

slides.title: Why Sliding Scale Insulin (SSI) Monotherapy Fails
bullets: SSI monotherapy reacts retrospectively to hyperglycemia and provides zero basal coverage, causing overnight and pre-meal spikes.
RABBIT 2 (n=130 medical T2DM) showed basal-bolus achieved BG < 140 mg/dL in 66% vs. 38% with SSI.
RABBIT 2 Surgery (n=211) showed basal-bolus cut composite postoperative complications nearly two-thirds (8.6% vs. 24.3%, p=0.003).
Correctional-only insulin is acceptable only for mild stress hyperglycemia (140-180 mg/dL); escalate if required > 2 times in 24 hours.

chart_spec.title: RABBIT 2 & RABBIT 2 Surgery: Basal-Bolus vs. Sliding Scale (SSI)

slides.speaker_notes: Evidence Base: Umpierrez et al., Diabetes Care 2007 (RABBIT 2) and Diabetes Care 2011 (RABBIT 2 Surgery). Attending Pearl: Frame SSI monotherapy to interns as putting out a kitchen fire only after the smoke alarm goes off, instead of turning off the stove.

slides.title: Pharmacokinetics of Inpatient Insulins
bullets: Rapid-acting analogs (lispro, aspart, glulisine) onset in 10-15 min, peak 1-2 hr, and last 3-5 hr.
Regular insulin onsets in 30-60 min, peaks 2-4 hr, and lasts 5-8 hr; used for IV drips and TPN.
NPH onsets in 1-2 hr, peaks 4-8 hr, and lasts 12-18 hr; ideal for morning prednisone and tube feeds.
Glargine U-100 lasts 20-24 hr peakless; degludec lasts 36-42+ hr and takes 3-4 days for steady state.
U-500 regular insulin exhibits dual prandial and basal kinetics; always dispense dedicated U-500 syringes or pens.
slides.speaker_notes: Evidence Base: ADA Pharmacologic Approaches and ISMP High-Alert Medication Safety Guidelines. Attending Pearl: U-500 insulin is a major inpatient safety hazard. Never draw U-500 into a U-100 syringe. Confirm dedicated U-500 syringes or KwikPen, or convert temporarily to U-100 basal-bolus at 80% of home TDD if intake is unpredictable.

slides.title: Managing Home Non-Insulin Agents on Admission
bullets: Discontinue most oral and non-insulin injectable agents on admission and transition to scheduled insulin.
Weekly GLP-1 RAs remain active for 5-7 days after holding, blunting postprandial excursions.
DPP-4 inhibitors may be continued with basal insulin in stable non-ICU T2DM with BG < 200 mg/dL.

table.title: Admission Disposition of Home Non-Insulin Diabetes Medications
rows: Risk of MALA in AKI, sepsis, hypoperfusion, or contrast with eGFR < 30
High risk of euglycemic DKA, volume depletion; may resume pre-discharge in stable HF
Prolonged severe hypoglycemia when meals are delayed, especially in CKD/elderly
Fluid retention, heart failure exacerbation, and slow onset/offset
Delayed gastric emptying worsens inpatient nausea and procedural aspiration risk
Sita-Hospital trial showed non-inferiority with basal insulin in mild-moderate T2DM

slides.speaker_notes: Evidence Base: Sita-Hospital Trial (Pasquel et al., Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2017) and Endocrine Society 2022 Guideline. Attending Pearl: Long-acting weekly GLP-1 RAs (semaglutide, tirzepatide) have a 5-7 day half-life; even when held, the drug remains active throughout hospitalization, increasing sensitivity to added prandial insulin.

slides.title: Calculating Total Daily Dose (TDD): Weight-Based and Home Conversions
bullets: High hypoglycemia risk (age > 70, eGFR < 45-60, frail, hepatic failure, new T1DM): start 0.2-0.3 units/kg/day.
Standard T2DM: start 0.4 units/kg/day for BG 140-200 mg/dL or 0.5 units/kg/day for BG > 200 mg/dL.
Severe insulin resistance (BMI > 35 kg/m2, high-dose steroids, severe sepsis): start 0.6 units/kg/day.
Split TDD into 50% basal insulin and 50% prandial insulin divided equally across three meals.
Reduce home basal insulin by 20%-25% on admission if poor appetite, NPO status, AKI, or HbA1c < 7.0%.
slides.speaker_notes: Evidence Base: ADA 2024/2025 Standards of Care and Endocrine Society 2022 Clinical Practice Guideline. Attending Pearl: Walk through a quick mental math example: An 80 kg, 58-year-old man with T2DM, normal creatinine, BG 240 mg/dL, eating well -> 0.5 units/kg = 40 units TDD -> 20 units glargine QHS + 7 units lispro TID AC + moderate correctional scale.

slides.title: Basal-Bolus vs. Basal-Plus Regimens
bullets: Basal-bolus-correction is preferred for patients with consistent oral intake and persistent BG > 180 mg/dL.
Basal-plus (basal plus correctional, no scheduled prandial) fits NPO, poor oral intake, or elderly/frail patients.
Basal-Plus Trial (n=375) showed glargine 0.25 units/kg plus correction was non-inferior to full basal-bolus.
For erratic appetite, dose rapid-acting insulin immediately post-meal: full dose if >= 50% eaten, half if 25%-50%, hold if < 25%.
slides.speaker_notes: Evidence Base: Basal-Plus Trial (Umpierrez et al., Diabetes Care 2013). Attending Pearl: Post-meal rapid-acting insulin dosing is one of the highest-yield practical safety tools on medicine wards for patients with nausea or fluctuating intake. Explicitly teach interns how to write clear nursing parameters for this order.

slides.title: Correctional Insulin Scales and Avoiding Insulin Stacking
bullets: Match correctional scale intensity to patient TDD, age, renal function, and steroid exposure.
Avoid dosing rapid-acting correctional insulin more often than every 4 hours to prevent insulin stacking.
Use conservative bedtime (QHS) correction (treat only if BG > 200 mg/dL at half dose) to avoid 03:00 AM hypoglycemia.
slides.speaker_notes: Evidence Base: ADA Inpatient Glycemic Safety Standards and SHM Glycemic Control Implementation Guide. Attending Pearl: Teach residents the 1800 Rule for estimating the Insulin Sensitivity Factor (ISF) in T1DM or complex patients: ISF = 1800 / TDD. If TDD = 45 units, 1 unit of rapid-acting insulin lowers BG by ~40 mg/dL.

slides.title: Daily Bedside Titration: Pattern Management for Morning Rounds
bullets: Attribute fasting BG to basal insulin, pre-lunch to breakfast bolus, pre-dinner to lunch bolus, and bedtime to dinner bolus.
Stabilize fasting BG first: increase basal by 10% for fasting 140-180 mg/dL or 20% for fasting > 180-200 mg/dL.
Alternatively, incorporate 50%-80% of prior 24-hour correctional insulin into scheduled basal or bolus doses.
After unexplained BG < 70 mg/dL, reduce responsible insulin by 20%; after BG < 54 mg/dL, reduce by 30%-50%.
Avoid over-basalization (> 0.5 units/kg/day or > 60% of TDD with normal fasting and high bedtime BG).
slides.speaker_notes: Evidence Base: RABBIT 2 Titration Protocol and SHM Inpatient Glycemic Control Resource Room. Attending Pearl: Emphasize the Rule of Over-Basalization: If basal exceeds 0.5 units/kg/day and fasting BG is 100-120 mg/dL while bedtime BG is 260 mg/dL, stop raising basal! Pushing basal causes nocturnal hypoglycemia (BeAM effect: Bedtime-to-Morning drop > 50 mg/dL); escalate prandial insulin instead.

slides.title: Managing the NPO Patient and Perioperative Glycemic Care
bullets: Hold SGLT2 inhibitors 3 days pre-op (4 days for ertugliflozin); hold metformin and sulfonylureas morning of surgery.
Per Oct 2024 Multi-Society GLP-1 guidance, stable patients may continue with a 24-hr liquid diet; hold if GI symptoms/escalation.
Give 75%-80% of usual long-acting basal insulin pre-op (never hold completely in T1DM) and 50% of morning NPH.
Hold prandial insulin while NPO, check POC BG q4-6h, and maintain perioperative BG between 100-180 mg/dL.
slides.speaker_notes: Evidence Base: ADA 2024/2025 Standards of Care; Endocrine Society 2022 Guideline; 2024 Multi-Society GLP-1 Perioperative Guidance (Oct 2024). Attending Pearl: A common intern error is holding all insulin at midnight when a patient is made NPO after midnight. Reinforce that basal insulin covers hepatic glucose output, not breakfast!

slides.title: Glucocorticoid-Induced Hyperglycemia
bullets: Morning prednisone peaks in 4-8 hours (afternoon/evening hyperglycemia) and wanes overnight, sparing morning fasting BG.
Administer NPH concurrently with morning prednisone: 0.1 U/kg per 10 mg prednisone up to 0.4 U/kg for >= 40 mg.
Long-acting or split-dose steroids (dexamethasone, BID methylprednisolone) require 24-hour basal-bolus with 30%-50% higher TDD.
Reduce steroid-targeted NPH or basal-bolus doses by 20%-50% on the exact day steroids are tapered or stopped.

chart_spec.title: Matching Morning Prednisone Excursion with Morning NPH

slides.speaker_notes: Evidence Base: Endocrine Society 2022 Inpatient Guideline; Umpierrez et al. steroid protocols; ADA 2024/2025. Attending Pearl: If a patient on morning prednisone receives escalating glargine instead of NPH to chase 17:00 BG spikes of 320 mg/dL, they will predictably crash into severe hypoglycemia at 04:00 AM when the prednisone wears off.

slides.title: Enteral Nutrition (Tube Feeds) and Total Parenteral Nutrition (TPN)
bullets: Continuous tube feeds: give basal insulin (glargine daily or NPH q8-12h at 40% TDD) plus regular q6h or rapid-acting q4h.
Cyclic nocturnal tube feeds: give NPH at feed start plus q4-6h correction; bolus feeds: give rapid-acting before each bolus.
TPN gold standard: add regular insulin to the TPN bag at 0.1 units per gram of dextrose (1 U per 10 g).
On TPN day 2, add 80% of prior 24-hour correctional insulin into the next day's TPN bag.
Safety protocol: if continuous tube feeds or TPN stop abruptly, immediately start IV D10W at the feed rate and check BG q1-2h.
slides.speaker_notes: Evidence Base: ASPEN Clinical Guidelines; ADA 2024/2025; Endocrine Society 2022. Attending Pearl: Make the D10W nursing order automatic! Whenever an intern orders basal insulin for continuous tube feeds, instruct them to enter a linked conditional order: If tube feeds are held > 1 hour, start D10W IV at the tube feed mL/hr rate and notify MD.

slides.title: Renal Impairment (CKD/ESRD) and Hepatic Failure
bullets: Kidneys clear 30%-50% of exogenous insulin and supply 20%-40% of fasting gluconeogenesis; eGFR < 45 prolongs insulin half-life.
Reduce initial TDD to 0.25-0.3 units/kg/day in CKD (reduce 25% if eGFR 10-50; 50% if eGFR < 10 or on HD).
Baldwin et al. (2012) showed lowering TDD from 0.5 to 0.25 U/kg/day in CKD halved hypoglycemia (15.8% vs. 30.0%).
Reduce basal insulin by 20%-25% on hemodialysis days due to post-dialysis insulin sensitivity.
Cirrhosis depletes hepatic glycogen and impairs gluconeogenesis; start 0.2-0.3 U/kg/day using rapid-acting analogs.
slides.speaker_notes: Evidence Base: Baldwin et al., Diabetes Care 2012. Attending Pearl: Watch out for acute kidney injury (AKI) developing mid-hospitalization! A sudden unexplained drop in morning glucose or recurrent hypoglycemia in a previously stable ward patient is often an early clinical clue to worsening AKI, occult sepsis, or adrenal insufficiency.

slides.title: Inpatient Diabetes Technology: Insulin Pumps, AID Systems, and CGMs
bullets: Alert, competent non-ICU patients may self-manage personal insulin pumps/AID systems if supplies and hospital policy allow.
Discontinue pumps and switch to SQ/IV insulin for delirium, DKA/HHS, ICU care, suicidal ideation, or MRI procedures.
Never disconnect a T1DM insulin pump without giving SQ basal insulin first or starting an IV insulin drip.
Personal CGMs may continue with mandatory fingerstick confirmation for BG < 70 or > 300 mg/dL, rapid change, or vasopressors.
Watch CGM interferences: hydroxyurea falsely elevates Dexcom/Medtronic; high-dose IV Vitamin C falsely elevates FreeStyle Libre.
slides.speaker_notes: Evidence Base: ADA 2024/2025 Standards of Care (Section 16) and Endocrine Society 2022 Guideline. Attending Pearl: Always document the patient's pump basal rates, insulin-to-carb ratio, and sensitivity factor in the admission note. Remember insulin pumps contain only rapid-acting insulin; once disconnected, zero basal insulin remains within 2-3 hours.

slides.title: Inpatient Hypoglycemia: Classification, Acute Rescue, and Prevention
bullets: ADA tiers: Level 1 is BG < 70 and >= 54 mg/dL; Level 2 < 54 mg/dL; Level 3 requires external assistance.
Awake patients: give 15-20 g oral fast-acting carbohydrate, recheck BG in 15 min, and repeat if still < 70 mg/dL.
NPO or altered patients with IV access: give 25-50 mL IV D50W (12.5-25 g) or 100-250 mL D10W; recheck in 15 min.
No IV access: give glucagon 1 mg IM/SQ or 3 mg intranasal (ineffective in severe cirrhosis or starvation).
Every Level 1-3 event mandates auditing triggers and reducing the offending insulin dose by 20%-30%.
slides.speaker_notes: Evidence Base: ADA 2024/2025 Standards of Care and NICE-SUGAR secondary analysis. Attending Pearl: Beware the Sulfonylurea Rebound Trap! In sulfonylurea overdose or AKI-induced hypoglycemia, IV D50W triggers an endogenous insulin surge causing recurrent hypoglycemia 1-2 hours later. Admit 24-48 hours, run continuous D10W, and give Octreotide 50-100 mcg SQ q6-8h.

slides.title: Diagnostic Criteria for DKA and HHS: 2024 Consensus Update
bullets: 2024 consensus lowered DKA glucose threshold to >= 200 mg/dL or prior diabetes to capture euglycemic DKA.
Euglycemic DKA is precipitated by SGLT2 inhibitors, pregnancy, prolonged fasting, alcohol use, or partial pre-hospital insulin.
Up to one-third of hyperglycemic crisis patients present with DKA/HHS overlap.

table.title: 2024 ADA/EASD/JBDS Diagnostic Criteria: DKA vs. HHS

slides.speaker_notes: Evidence Base: Umpierrez et al., Hyperglycemic Crises in Adults With Diabetes: A Consensus Report (Diabetes Care / Diabetologia, June 2024). Attending Pearl: Never rely solely on urine nitroprusside strips to track DKA resolution! Nitroprusside detects acetoacetate, not beta-hydroxybutyrate. As DKA resolves, beta-hydroxybutyrate oxidizes to acetoacetate, making urine ketones appear worse. Always order serum beta-hydroxybutyrate.

slides.title: Acute Resuscitation: Fluids, Electrolytes, and Potassium Safety Gates
bullets: Resuscitate volume first with balanced crystalloids (LR or Plasma-Lyte) or 0.9% NS at 500-1,000 mL/hr for 2-4 hours.
Switch to 0.45% NaCl at 250-500 mL/hr if corrected sodium is >= 135 mEq/L.
Potassium safety gate: if K+ < 3.5 mEq/L, HOLD insulin and infuse KCl 10-20 mEq/hr until K+ >= 3.5 mEq/L.
If K+ is 3.5-5.0 mEq/L, add 20-40 mEq KCl/L IVF; if K+ > 5.0 mEq/L, start insulin and recheck q2h.
Avoid routine bicarbonate unless pH < 7.0; replace phosphate only if < 1.0 mg/dL or cardiopulmonary weakness.
slides.speaker_notes: Evidence Base: 2024 ADA/EASD/JBDS Consensus Report; Self et al. (JAMA Netw Open 2020) showed balanced crystalloids accelerated DKA resolution by ~4 hours vs. 0.9% NS. Attending Pearl: In HHS, fluid resuscitation alone drops BG by 50-100 mg/dL/hr. Avoid dropping serum osmolality faster than 3-8 mOsm/kg/hr or Na+ faster than 10 mEq/L per 24 hours to prevent cerebral edema.

slides.title: IV Insulin Infusions, Dextrose Addition, and Resolution Criteria
bullets: Start DKA IV regular insulin at 0.1 units/kg/hr; start HHS at 0.05 units/kg/hr after initial fluid resuscitation.
Mild-to-moderate uncomplicated DKA may be treated with SQ rapid-acting analogs (0.1-0.2 U/kg q2-4h) in ED/step-down.
When DKA BG reaches < 250 mg/dL (or immediately in euDKA), add D5W/D10W and halve IV insulin to 0.05 units/kg/hr.
Check POC BG q1h and BMP, venous pH, and serum beta-hydroxybutyrate q2-4h.
DKA resolution requires ALL: beta-hydroxybutyrate < 0.6 mmol/L, pH >= 7.3 or HCO3- >= 18 mmol/L, and BG < 200 mg/dL.
slides.speaker_notes: Evidence Base: 2024 ADA/EASD/JBDS Hyperglycemic Crises Consensus Report. Attending Pearl: Teach residents about early basal insulin co-administration: giving SQ glargine (0.15-0.3 units/kg) within the first 12 hours of the IV insulin infusion accelerates DKA resolution, prevents rebound hyperglycemia, and shortens ICU length of stay without increasing hypoglycemia (Hsia et al. 2012; Thammakosol et al. 2023).

slides.title: Transitioning Off the IV Insulin Drip: The 2-Hour Overlap and Math
bullets: IV insulin half-life is 5-7 minutes while SQ basal takes 1-2 hours; stopping simultaneously triggers rebound DKA.
Administer SQ basal insulin 2 hours BEFORE discontinuing the IV insulin infusion.
Drip-rate method: multiply average stable hourly IV rate by 24 hours, take 60%-80% as TDD, split 50% basal / 50% prandial.
Home-regimen or weight-based (0.3-0.5 units/kg/day) methods are valid alternatives depending on prior control.
Check POC BG 2 hours after stopping the drip and then AC/QHS to confirm smooth glycemic handoff.

Simultaneous Stop at t=0 (Rebound DKA Risk)

annotations.text: Safe to Stop IV Drip (t = 2 hr)

slides.speaker_notes: Evidence Base: ADA 2024/2025 Standards of Care and 2024 Hyperglycemic Crises Consensus Report. Attending Pearl: Walk through morning ICU math: Stable IV rate over last 6 hours is 2 units/hr. 2 x 24 = 48 units/day. Take 70%-80% (~36 units TDD) -> give 18 units glargine SQ at 08:00, stop IV drip at 10:00, and start 6 units lispro TID AC + correction.

slides.title: HbA1c-Guided Discharge Medication Reconciliation
bullets: HbA1c < 7.0%: resume pre-admission outpatient regimen after verifying renal safety for metformin and SGLT2 inhibitors.
HbA1c 7.0%-9.0%: resume safe oral agents and intensify with SGLT2i/GLP-1 RA or 50% of hospital basal dose.
HbA1c > 9.0%-10.0%: discharge on basal-bolus (80% hospital TDD) or basal (80% hospital basal) plus oral/GLP-1 therapy.
Reduce hospital basal insulin by 10%-20% at discharge if severe infection or high-dose steroids are resolving.
Provide an explicit written insulin taper schedule when discharging on a short glucocorticoid taper.

chart_spec.title: HbA1c-Stratified Discharge Insulin Intensification
chart_spec.y_label: Hospital Insulin Dose Carried to Discharge (%)

slides.speaker_notes: Evidence Base: Umpierrez et al. (Diabetes Care 2014) showed admission HbA1c-guided discharge reduced HbA1c by 1.5%-2.2% at 12 weeks safely; ADA 2024/2025. Attending Pearl: Inpatient insulin resistance resolves rapidly once home after infection or inflammation clears, so a 10%-20% basal reduction prevents post-discharge hypoglycemia.

slides.title: Essential Discharge Logistics, Education, and Reducing 30-Day Readmissions
bullets: Up to 20% of hospitalized diabetes patients are readmitted within 30 days due to medication errors and missing supplies.
Verify formulary coverage with pharmacy and prescribe five essentials: insulin, pen needles/syringes, glucometer/strips/lancets, glucagon, and sharps disposal.
Pen needles (4 mm x 32G) or syringes are the most frequently forgotten discharge prescription.
Teach survival skills: Rule-of-15 hypoglycemia rescue, injection technique, and T1DM sick-day rules.
Schedule outpatient primary care or endocrinology follow-up within 1-2 weeks for new/modified insulin or DKA/HHS.
slides.speaker_notes: Evidence Base: ADA 2024/2025 Standards of Care (Section 16) and SHM Project BOOST / Glycemic Transitions Toolkit. Attending Pearl: Remind residents to check formulary tiering before writing for brand-name glargine versus biosimilar insulin glargine-yfgn or degludec so patients do not abandon prescriptions at the pharmacy due to high copays.

slides.title: Interactive Tiered Resident Case Vignettes (PGY-1, PGY-2, PGY-3)

cards.title: Case 1 (PGY-1): Ward Admission & TDD
items: 68F (70 kg), T2DM, HbA1c 8.4%, AKI (Cr 1.9, eGFR 28), BG 254 mg/dL, eating 75%.
Hold metformin (AKI, eGFR < 30); avoid SSI monotherapy.
CKD/age: 0.3 U/kg/day = 21 U TDD (10 U glargine QHS, 3-4 U lispro TID AC, Low-Dose scale).

cards.title: Case 2 (PGY-2): Steroids & NPO
items: 62M (80 kg), T1DM (glargine 22 U, lispro 6 U TID) on prednisone 40 mg AM; NPO; PM BG 295, AM 105.
NPO: NEVER hold T1DM basal; give 80% (18 U glargine QHS), hold AM bolus, add D5 1/2 NS if BG < 150.
When eating on prednisone 40 mg: add AM NPH (20-24 U at 08:00) rather than raising glargine.

cards.title: Case 3 (PGY-3): Euglycemic DKA
items: 54M, T2DM on empagliflozin, post-op; BG 178 mg/dL, HCO3- 11, K+ 3.2 mEq/L, pH 7.18, beta-OHB 4.8.
SGLT2i euDKA: HOLD IV insulin for K+ < 3.5 mEq/L; replete KCl until K+ >= 3.5 mEq/L.
Start IV insulin 0.1 U/kg/hr + D5W/D10W; overlap SQ basal 2 hours before stopping drip.

slides.speaker_notes: Attending Pearl: Call on interns for Case 1, PGY-2s for Case 2, and PGY-3s for Case 3 to keep all training levels actively engaged and psychologically safe. Emphasize potassium-first safety in Case 3 and permanent documentation of SGLT2i peri-procedural hold risk.

slides.title: High-Yield Summary: The Attending's 5 Golden Rules
bullets: Target the safe middle: 140-180 mg/dL in ICU and 100-180 mg/dL on floor; hypoglycemia kills faster than mild hyperglycemia.
Never starve T1DM of basal insulin: NPO means reduce basal by 20% and add dextrose IVF if needed.
Bury sliding scale monotherapy: use weight-based basal-bolus or basal-plus and titrate daily via 4-point patterns.
Respect high-risk curves: NPH for prednisone, 0.25-0.3 U/kg in CKD, D10W for tube feeds, K+ gate, 2-hr DKA overlap.
Discharge with precision: check HbA1c, verify formulary coverage, prescribe needles/glucometer/glucagon, and book 1-2 week follow-up.
slides.speaker_notes: Attending Pearl: End the presentation by distributing a pocket card or QR code to the hospital's electronic glycemic order set so residents immediately apply the session's calculations during afternoon admissions.

handout_sections.title: Glycemic Targets, TDD Dosing, and Daily Titration
handout_sections.summary: Core inpatient targets, T1DM basal safety, weight-based TDD initiation, and daily 4-point pattern titration.
rules: Initiate insulin for persistent hyperglycemia >= 180 mg/dL on two occasions within 24 hours.
Target BG 140-180 mg/dL in ICU and 100-180 mg/dL on non-ICU floors (< 200-250 mg/dL if terminally ill).
Check admission HbA1c if no result exists within 3 months (diabetes >= 6.5%).
NEVER withhold basal insulin completely in T1DM; reduce by 20% when NPO and start D5 1/2 NS if BG drops.
Weight-based TDD: 0.2-0.3 units/kg/day (CKD eGFR < 45, age > 70, frail, hepatic failure), 0.4-0.5 units/kg/day (standard T2DM), 0.6 units/kg/day (BMI > 35, high-dose steroids).
Split TDD 50% basal / 50% prandial; use Basal-Plus (basal + correction) for NPO or poor PO intake.
Hypoglycemia tiers: Level 1 (< 70 mg/dL and >= 54 mg/dL) and Level 2 (< 54 mg/dL). Reduce responsible insulin by 20%-50% after any event.

handout_sections.title: High-Risk Scenarios and 2024 DKA/HHS Protocol
handout_sections.summary: Perioperative holds, glucocorticoid NPH matching, enteral/TPN safety, and 2024 ADA/EASD/JBDS DKA/HHS resuscitation.
rules: Hold SGLT2 inhibitors 3 days pre-op (4 days for ertugliflozin); hold metformin and sulfonylureas morning of surgery; give 75%-80% basal insulin pre-op.
Match morning prednisone with morning NPH (0.1 U/kg per 10 mg up to 0.4 U/kg for >= 40 mg); cut dose 20%-50% on the exact day steroids taper.
Enteral/TPN safety: add 0.1 U regular insulin per gram of dextrose in TPN; order conditional IV D10W if continuous tube feeds stop abruptly.
2024 DKA criteria: BG >= 200 mg/dL or prior diabetes, beta-hydroxybutyrate >= 3.0 mmol/L, and pH < 7.3 or HCO3- < 18 mmol/L.
2024 HHS criteria: BG >= 600 mg/dL, effective osmolality > 300 mOsm/kg, beta-hydroxybutyrate < 3.0 mmol/L, pH >= 7.3 and HCO3- >= 15 mmol/L.
Potassium safety gate: if K+ < 3.5 mEq/L, HOLD insulin and infuse KCl 10-20 mEq/hr until K+ >= 3.5 mEq/L.
DKA IV regular insulin: 0.1 units/kg/hr (HHS: 0.05 units/kg/hr). When BG < 250 mg/dL (or immediately in euDKA), add D5W/D10W and halve insulin to 0.05 units/kg/hr.
DKA resolution: beta-hydroxybutyrate < 0.6 mmol/L, pH >= 7.3 or HCO3- >= 18 mmol/L, and BG < 200 mg/dL. Overlap SQ basal insulin 2 hours before stopping IV drip.

handout_sections.title: Inpatient-to-Discharge Transition Checklist and Clinical Pearls
handout_sections.summary: HbA1c-guided discharge intensification, 5 essential discharge prescriptions, survival skills, and 60-second morning rounds audit.
rules: Morning Rounds 60-Second Audit: scan 24-hr min/max BG, verify PO intake, check creatinine/AKI, confirm steroid tapers, and verify D10W order for tube feeds.
Reduce hospital basal insulin by 10%-20% at discharge if acute infection, inflammation, or high-dose steroids are resolving.
Clinical Pearl: Beware the Sulfonylurea Rebound Trap—treat AKI/sulfonylurea hypoglycemia with continuous D10W and Octreotide 50-100 mcg SQ q6-8h.
Clinical Pearl: Never track DKA resolution with urine nitroprusside strips; always order serum beta-hydroxybutyrate.
Prescribe all 5 discharge essentials: formulary-verified insulin, pen needles/syringes, glucometer/strips/lancets, rescue glucagon, and sharps disposal.
Schedule outpatient primary care or endocrinology follow-up within 1-2 weeks for new/modified insulin or recent DKA/HHS.
